email.body1:
Alison, saw Trusaic shipped the Workday PayParity integration and expanded into Europe ahead of the EU Pay Transparency deadline.

Riding a regulatory wave usually means more enterprise accounts in play than the team can cover before new reps ramp, and that is where deals go cold. Our AI SDR researches, writes, and follows up autonomously, so coverage scales without new headcount: 3-5x more meetings per rep.

I built a personalized signal play for Trusaic off your hiring and tech-stack signals, and accounts showing them tend to progress ~4.4x faster. Worth 15 minutes for me to walk you through it?
email.body2:
Alison, quick follow-up for Trusaic.

With the EU deadline driving demand, the pipeline expectation on enterprise BD climbs faster than headcount can. Most teams don't actually know how many meetings they need booked to capture that window, so the gap shows up late in the quarter.

Want to grab 15 minutes? I'll walk you through our pipeline model and show exactly how many meetings your team needs to hit target, and where the math breaks if you only add reps.
email.body3:
Alison, last bit of proof for Trusaic.

Memgraph had more in-market accounts than the team could touch and couldn't hire SDRs fast enough. They ran our AI SDR to $2.7M in pipeline, 600 replies, and 60 BANT-qualified deals in 90 days, same team, live in four weeks, every email auto-logged to CRM.

I pulled a benchmark of how Trusaic's reply rate likely compares to other enterprise HR-tech teams. Want to hop on a quick call and I'll walk you through it?
email.body4:
Alison, I'll stop reaching out on this one, but didn't want to leave you empty-handed.

If scaling enterprise pipeline without adding headcount isn't a priority this quarter, no problem at all. Capturing a regulatory-driven window across two regions is its own kind of busy.

Before I close your file, worth 15 minutes to walk through a one-page playbook of three AI-SDR plays scoped to an enterprise motion? I'll tailor it to Trusaic either way.
